newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China says must investigate Korean defector issue.
newsitem.headline: China says must investigate Korean defector issue.

text.p: Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda raised the issue of a North Korean defector with Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen at talks late on Friday, but there were no signs of progress on the matter.
Asked whether Ikeda and Qian talked about the defector, Chinese spokesman Guo Chong-li told reporters: "Mr Ikeda did raise this issue and they did exchange information."

But Guo said that did not count as "official discussions", and repeated earlier statements that Beijing needed more time to decide on the fate of the top Pyongyang defector, Hwang Jang-yop, holed up in Seouls Beijing embassy.
"Its still premature to say how the case will be resolved. There are all kinds of suggestions about this issue from the two Koreas and other parties," Guo said.
He said China intended to seriously investigate the matter. "After all facts have been clarified we will talk about how to solve the case."

Earlier on Friday Qian met with his South Korean counterpart Yoo Chong-ha, and said afterwards that Hwangs defection had surprised China. "This incident happened all of a sudden, so we need more time to investigate," Qian said.
Qian, Yoo and Ikeda were in Singapore for meetings of European and Asian foreign ministers.
Hwang, 73, was a pillar of North Koreas Stalinist establishment, and a senior aide to North Korean leader Kim Jong-il.

The defection -- Pyongyang called it a kidnapping -- has dragged China into a heated row that has bred fears of renewed tension on the Korean peninsula and possibly a disastrous collapse of the North.
South Korea is urging China to allow Hwang, whom it said walked into its Beijing embassy on Wednesday after arriving with an aide by taxi to claim political asylum, to go to Seoul.
North Korea is demanding that China return Hwang, credited with helping to devise Pyongyangs quirky brand of socialism.
That leaves Beijing the choice of offending its old socialist comrade or a new capitalist partner that is investing heavily in China's booming economy.
